'''Mobicom Corporation''' ({{langx|mn|Мобиком Корпораци}}) is the largest [[mobile phone]] operator in [[Mongolia]].

It was  established as a joint Mongolian-Japanese venture on 18 March 1996, to be the first Mongolian cell phone service. It was founded by [[Newcom Group]], [[Sumitomo Corporation]], and [[KDDI]]. Mongolia's Newcom. In 2016 March, Mobicom was consolidated in KDDI Corporation Group and KDDI took majority share.

As of June, 2015, Mobicom holds over 33 percent of the mobile service market,<ref>{{cite web |title = Statistics 2015|publisher = Mongolian Telecommunications Regulatory Committee|url = http://crc.gov.mn/k/35/23|accessdate = 2015-03-23}}</ref>. It delivers its services through 64 branch units, 2,200 dealers and over 10,000 mobile sales points.

Aside from cellular communications, Mobicom also has services including international communications, Internet and satellite communications and wireless local loop or WLL.<ref>{{cite web | title = About us | publisher = Mobicom | url = http://www.mobicom.mn/index.jsp?mmid=1 | accessdate = 2008-04-10 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080410195658/http://www.mobicom.mn/index.jsp?mmid=1 | archive-date = 2008-04-10 | url-status = dead }}</ref>  Its prepaid services are exclusively sold through Newtel LLC.

Mobicom introduced [[3.5G]] networking in 2009, and provides [[High Speed Packet Access|HSPA]]. However it was initially late to 3G, 4G and 5G compared to other telecom companies such as Unitel.

Mobicom network supports phones with UMTS 2100, HSDPA 2100, HSUPA 2100, HSPA 2100, 3G, 3.5G, LTE, VoLTE, 4G+, and 5G.
